requests are never traced. Local development keeps 100% sampling by default.
`TRACE_SAMPLING_RATIO` accepts a value from `0` through `1` when an explicit
runtime override is needed.

For a short staging investigation, manually dispatch `Deploy Scaleway staging`
with `full_trace_debugging` enabled. That deployment samples 100% of application
traces for all three roles. Dispatch the next forward deployment without that
option to restore the Terraform-owned 10% value.

Use [LATENCY_MONITORING.md](LATENCY_MONITORING.md) for warm-path objectives,
external synthetic checks, trace dashboards, alert thresholds, and latency
incident response. Application-side improvement work is ordered in
[../../LATENCY_IMPROVEMENT.md](../../LATENCY_IMPROVEMENT.md).
The temporary `Monitor staging latency` workflow has a manual trigger only.
Scaleway operational work is deferred; resume these checks only when that work
is explicitly resumed. Successful staging deployments retain a separate
10-sample report-only baseline in their deployment evidence.

## DNS and Transactional Email

Keep Cloudflare as the authoritative DNS provider. Terraform manages only the
unproxied `staging.evorto.app` CNAME, the SPF, DKIM, MX, and DMARC records for
`notifications.evorto.app`, and the unproxied `alpha.evorto.app` CNAME after the
production root is explicitly applied. It does not transfer or otherwise manage
the zone itself. Each environment exposes `managed_dns_record`; bootstrap
exposes `managed_transactional_email_dns_records`.

The Scaleway custom-domain resources explicitly depend on their Cloudflare
CNAME records. This ordering lets the public CNAME propagate before Scaleway
starts its HTTP-01 challenge and certificate issuance during a fresh apply.

All other existing zone records remain intentionally outside this Terraform
state and must be preserved. This includes the apex, `www`, and `docs` website
records; Microsoft 365 mail and autodiscovery records; the `messages` Mailgun
records; Productlane and Azure custom-domain records; and their verification
records. A Terraform apply in this directory neither imports nor deletes those
records.

The legacy Fly A, AAAA, and ACME records for `alpha.evorto.app` were removed
after preserving a zone export. Alpha intentionally has no DNS record until the
production root is explicitly reviewed and applied by the operator. That apply
creates only the Scaleway CNAME; export and inspect the live zone again before
cutover, and never use a bulk zone replacement.

After the managed records have propagated and Scaleway reports the email domain
healthy, set `validate_tem_dns = true`. The application always sends as
`Evorto <no-reply@notifications.evorto.app>` and retains tenant-specific
Reply-To headers.

Serverless Containers currently support at most 50 custom domains per
container. The one-host-per-environment design is below that limit, but any
future move to direct per-tenant container domains requires a scaling decision
before the limit is approached.

## Deployment and recovery

`scaleway-staging.yml` runs after an eligible protected baseline or a manual
dispatch. It never cancels an active deployment. It:

1. proves that the exact main SHA passed both release gates;
2. builds Linux/amd64 once as `sha-<full-sha>` or reuses its immutable manifest;
3. verifies the runtime image, schema hash, SBOM, vulnerabilities, and size;
4. requires an empty read-only Terraform plan, then reconciles role-scoped
   secrets;
5. deploys private ops, rejects a destructive Drizzle plan, and applies the
   stable plan; initializes deterministic staging data only when every
   application table is empty, and otherwise preserves the existing data;
6. deploys worker and web at the same digest;
7. verifies health, readiness, version identity, tenant resolution, Auth0/RPC,
   and staging `noindex` behavior;
8. writes an immutable deployment manifest and updates the versioned latest
   pointer only after success.

If any forward-deploy check fails, the workflow remains visibly failed and does
not update the successful manifest pointer. It never redeploys an older image
after a schema release. Apply a reviewed infrastructure change explicitly or
ship a corrected forward revision, then rerun the deployment.

The production workflow is dispatch-only. Set `PRODUCTION_ENABLED` on the
protected `scaleway-production` GitHub environment. After environment approval,
the first validation step requires its value to be exactly `true`; a false,
missing, or other value fails the job before external commands. Environment
variables are available only after the job starts, so this check belongs in the
protected step rather than the job condition. The workflow then accepts only an
immutable, successful staging manifest for the current canonical `main` SHA.
The workflow must itself be dispatched from that revision on `main`; queued
older dispatches and reruns fail the fresh revision check. It copies the exact
accepted digest into the production registry without rebuilding, requires an
empty read-only production Terraform plan, then rechecks canonical `main`
immediately before reconciling production secrets and deploying the ops role.
It applies a safe schema plan, deploys worker/web, and smokes `alpha.evorto.app`.

These revision checks prevent selecting an older accepted release through this
workflow. They do not establish compatibility with an already-applied schema
or protect against out-of-band changes or rewritten branch history. The schema
explain/apply checks and coordinated compatibility review remain required.

Both the managed database instance and the application database declare
`prevent_destroy`. This blocks Terraform destruction or replacement while their
resource blocks remain in the configuration; removing a resource block also
removes its protection and requires explicit data-retention review. The protected
staging reset workflow resets and seeds through its private ops endpoint without
removing either Terraform database resource.

## Operational drills

Record every drill in the deployment metadata bucket under a unique timestamped
key. Evidence must include actor, start/end timestamps, source revision/digest,
commands or console operation IDs, observed result, and follow-up owner.

### Restore

1. Select a staging automatic backup and restore it to a new temporary private
   PostgreSQL instance; never overwrite the active database for the drill.
2. Attach a temporary private ops container or otherwise use a private-network
   schema identity to verify TLS, required extensions, schema hash, row counts,
   and representative tenant/registration/finance records.
3. Measure and record elapsed restoration time. The current commitment is a
   tested measurement, not an unproven RTO.
4. Delete the temporary restore only after the evidence object exists.

Run this before staging acceptance, quarterly, and after material backup or
schema changes. Staging retains daily backups for seven days. The production
root declares daily backups retained 30 days and a 24-hour RPO.

### Drift detection

1. Make one harmless, documented staging-only drift change such as a container
   description/tag through the console.
2. Dispatch the staging workflow for the current accepted revision and confirm
   its read-only Terraform plan reports the drift and stops before deployment.
3. Review and apply the matching staging root explicitly from the operator
   workstation.
4. Rerun the deployment, store the plan and `/version` evidence, and confirm the
   plan is empty apart from workflow-owned ignored fields.

### Forward recovery

1. Retain the failed workflow, image, schema, and smoke evidence.
2. Correct the defect in a new revision without reversing the applied schema.
3. Run the full local release gate and deploy that forward revision through the
   normal protected workflow.
4. Verify `/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/version`, SSR, and one RPC call, then record
   both the failed and corrected identities.

## Credential rotation

- Scaleway deployer, state, S3 role, and TEM API keys: every 90 days and after
  any suspected exposure or operator departure.
- application session secret: every 90 days with a planned sign-in reset;
- database passwords: every 90 days as a coordinated maintenance operation.
  Review and explicitly apply the password secret and matching incremented
  password-version variable in the environment infrastructure root, then run
  the protected forward deployment to reconcile runtime secrets and verify
  connectivity. Deployment workflows reject infrastructure changes in their
  read-only plans. Never reuse or decrement a version;
- Stripe webhook secret: whenever the endpoint is recreated or exposure is
  suspected;
- Auth0 and other provider credentials: follow provider guidance, at least
  annually, and immediately on suspected exposure.

Use overlap where the provider supports multiple active keys. Reconcile the new
value, verify the exact deployed revision/digest and a functional smoke test,
then revoke the old key. Never print current or replacement values in logs.

## Goal and scope

Main runs tests and deploys automatically to the existing Scaleway staging environment. Production is not provisioned and is outside this work. Owner: Codex in the staging-deployment chat, coordinated under Lukas. Related migration work: EVO-55; this change does not migrate CI to RWX.

## Final approach

- Give routine E2E Baseline its own main-only environment with no manual approval. Keep live-provider certification separate.
- Start staging eligibility checks when either PR Quality or E2E Baseline completes; deploy only when both passed on the current main SHA. Recheck exact-SHA job gates before deployment.
- Load an immutable private staging configuration snapshot, verified by digest and staging/project/role/database invariants. Routine releases no longer run Terraform or need Cloudflare/DNS or Terraform-state credentials.
- Keep image/SBOM scanning, safe schema explain/apply, identical ops/worker/web image digests, health/version/tenant checks and append-only deployment evidence.
- Infrastructure drift inspection is an explicit operator responsibility, separated from application release. The proposed three-root Terraform split remains unapplied; no state migration or production setup is part of this repair.

## Prepared and configured

Local commit e6bcbd83c56 on codex/evo-65-automatic-staging contains the workflows, configuration validator, 20 regression tests, documentation and Knope change file.

Created e2e-baseline with a main-only branch policy, 15 test credentials, no reviewer and no wait timer. Configured the actual staging project ID and immutable STAGING_CONFIGURATION_KEY. Published and read-back-verified configuration/staging/6c420761daf686560ba1c8be3d052c29e47ea0d17eb990f951313f7f4ba6f7aa.json in the private staging metadata bucket. The snapshot contains infrastructure metadata, secret IDs and public CA material, not secret values. Temporary inspection/publication keys were revoked after use.

The existing web/worker/ops containers are ready. Web currently runs d117229d3d7d357af9f9fc61fdad8d348d6809ea. Existing evorto/platform.tfstate serial 3060 was read and privately backed up; it was not modified. No DNS editing token is required for the final approach.

## Verification

Use pinned Node 24.22.1 (system 24.18.0 causes unrelated IPv6/TLS test failures). Completed: frozen install, lint (three existing warnings), formatting, Knope validation, server suite 174 files / 2716 tests, client suite 143 files / 1718 tests, PostgreSQL integration 34 files / 387 tests. All collected tests in these successful runs passed without incomplete outcomes. Infrastructure validation, image security/build and complete Playwright baseline are in progress/pending. Focused tests alone are not publication evidence.

## Remaining acceptance

Finish the full local gate before push/PR or Trail branch publication. Request Copilot review and address actionable findings. Keep the staging workflow disabled until the reviewed workflow lands on main, then enable it and observe a successful current-main baseline/deployment. Do not report the task complete before deployment and smoke evidence. No code has been pushed, no PR has been created, and no deployment has been triggered yet.

## Links

Entire intent: https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/9

## Goal and scope

Main runs tests and deploys automatically to the existing Scaleway staging environment. Production is not provisioned. Owner: Codex in this chat, coordinated under Lukas. Related work: EVO-55; RWX migration is outside this change.

Finish local verification before publishing. Create the linked PR, request Copilot review, address actionable findings and satisfy required checks. input.title: Make generated worktree ports compatible with Auth0-backed verification
input.description:
## Problem and evidence

A fresh worktree at /Users/hedde/.codex/worktrees/74da/evorto resolves APP_HOST_PORT=4520 and BASE_URL=http://localhost:4520. The canonical full browser baseline starts its exact Docker stack successfully, then authentication setup waits for a username field until timeout. A read-only authorization probe confirms Auth0 returns 403 Callback URL mismatch for http://localhost:4520/callback, while http://localhost:4200/callback is accepted (302 to /u/login). No Auth0 client settings were changed.

## Current workaround

Run the complete canonical baseline with APP_HOST_PORT=4200 and BASE_URL=http://localhost:4200 after coordinating ownership of that port. In EVO-65, an existing demo web container was temporarily stopped and will be restored by an EXIT trap; its database and other services were preserved. This workaround is environment configuration, not reduced test collection.

## Goal and acceptance

Choose a supported callback/origin strategy for generated worktree ports without exposing credentials or weakening ref protections. Preflight must fail clearly before building/seeding if the selected origin is unsupported. Verify a fresh worktree can run the unfiltered baseline without taking over an unrelated local app's port. Preserve frozen secret handling, exact-checkout verification and existing Auth0 production/staging callback restrictions.

## Scope

Follow-up only; not implemented under EVO-65. Coordinate with EVO-52 test workflow simplification. The available Auth0 management test client can read/update test users but cannot read client settings (403); changing those settings needs the appropriate operator context.

input.head: codex/evo-65-automatic-staging
input.title: fix: simplify automatic staging deployments (EVO-65)
input.body:
Merges to `main` should run tests and deploy to staging without a certification approval. Give routine E2E its own main-only environment, and check staging eligibility after either quality workflow finishes; both checks and their exact-SHA jobs must pass before deployment.

Routine deployment now loads a private immutable configuration snapshot, verifies its digest and staging/project/role/database invariants, and uses the existing infrastructure. It no longer runs Terraform or needs Cloudflare/DNS, state credentials or production identities. Infrastructure drift inspection becomes an explicit operator task. Image scanning, safe schema explain/apply, identical ops/worker/web image digests, smoke checks and append-only deployment evidence remain. There is no application schema change or production provisioning in this PR.

The test environment, staging project setting and accepted configuration object/pointer are prepared. Staging Actions remain disabled until this reviewed workflow is merged; activation and a successful current-main deployment are the remaining operational acceptance.

Validation on the committed tree with pinned Node 24.22.1: frozen install, lint/format and Knope validation; 2,716 server tests, 1,718 client tests, 387 PostgreSQL integration tests, and all 277 functional/documentation browser tests passed without incomplete outcomes. Infrastructure validation/security scanning and the Linux/amd64 runtime build, runtime verification, SBOM and vulnerability scan passed. The browser gate used the registered localhost:4200 origin; its original demo container was restored afterward. Generated-port/Auth0 preflight follow-up is EVO-66.

[Linear EVO-65](https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-65/restore-automatic-main-to-staging-deployments-without-certification) · [Entire Trail 9](https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/9)

Main runs tests and deploys automatically to the existing Scaleway staging environment. Production is not provisioned. Owner: Codex in this chat, coordinated under Lukas. Related work: <issue id="e4093133-bf43-42b2-a616-f807e8aa0d5e" label="EVO-55" href="https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-55/rebuild-release-certification-and-scaleway-delivery-on-rwx" />; RWX migration is outside this change.

## Implementation

Local commit `e6bcbd83c56` on `codex/evo-65-automatic-staging`:

* Routine E2E uses its own main-only environment without approval.
* Either quality workflow completion checks eligibility; both must pass on current main. Exact-SHA job gates are rechecked before deployment.
* Staging loads a private, immutable configuration snapshot verified by digest, project, role identities, endpoints and private database TLS settings.
* No Terraform, Terraform state credentials, Cloudflare token or production identity is needed for routine releases. Infrastructure drift inspection moves to explicit operator maintenance; image, schema and deployment health checks remain.
* Includes 20 regression tests, documentation and a Knope change file.

The prior proposal to migrate Terraform state is withdrawn. The live single state remains untouched; no production infrastructure or DNS was changed. The proposed three-root topology remains unapplied and requires a separate reviewed migration if ever pursued.

## Configured

Created `e2e-baseline` with 15 test credentials, only the main branch allowed, no reviewers and no wait timer. Set the actual staging project ID and immutable configuration pointer. Published and read-back-verified `configuration/staging/6c420761daf686560ba1c8be3d052c29e47ea0d17eb990f951313f7f4ba6f7aa.json` in the private staging metadata bucket. The snapshot contains metadata/secret IDs/CA material, never credential values. Temporary inspection/publication keys were revoked.

Ready web/worker/ops containers exist; web runs `d117229d3d7d357af9f9fc61fdad8d348d6809ea`. Remote state `evorto/platform.tfstate`, serial 3060, was privately backed up and not modified.

## Verification and remaining work

Pinned Node 24.22.1 resolves the unrelated IPv6/TLS failures seen with system Node 24.18.0.

All collected tests passed without incomplete outcomes. Complete Playwright baseline passed: all 277 tests, without retries or incomplete outcomes. The original demo web container was restored.

Finish local verification before publishing. Create the linked PR, request Copilot review, address actionable findings and satisfy required checks.
